tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0042_add_email_index.sql
  4  MG002  error    CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY blocks all writes to
                     users for the duration of the build.
                     statement: CREATE INDEX users_email_idx ON users (email)
                     fix: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY users_email_idx ON users
                          (email); run it outside a transaction.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0043_cleanup.sql
  1  MG004  error    DROP TABLE removes audit_legacy and its data permanently.
                     statement: DROP TABLE audit_legacy
                     fix: Stop reading and writing audit_legacy, ship that
                          version, then drop it in a later migration once the
                          previous release is retired.
  3  MG004  error    DROP COLUMN removes legacy_flag from users permanently, and
                     the previous release may still read it.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_flag
                     fix: Stop writing legacy_flag, ship that version, then drop
                          it in a later migration once no running code selects
                          it.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0045_widen_email.sql
  2  MG001  error    Changing the type of users.email rewrites the whole table
                     under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which blocks reads as well
                     as writes.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email TYPE varchar(255)
                     fix: Add a new column of the target type, backfill it in
                          batches, switch the application over, then drop the
                          old one; users.email stays readable throughout.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0046_add_status.sql
  2  MG003  error    ADD COLUMN status NOT NULL without a DEFAULT fails on users
                     as soon as it holds a single row.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status text NOT NULL
                     fix: Add status nullable, backfill it in batches, then
                          enforce it with CHECK (status IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID,
                          VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, and SET NOT NULL; or give this
                          statement a constant DEFAULT.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0047_enforce_email.sql
  2  MG001  error    SET NOT NULL on users.email takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and
                     scans every row before it returns.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL
                     fix: Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, VALIDATE
                          CONSTRAINT it in a later migration, then SET NOT NULL:
                          PostgreSQL 16 skips the scan when a validated check
                          already proves it.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0048_rename_email.sql
  2  MG005  error    Renaming users.email to primary_email removes the old name
                     while the previous release is still selecting it.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN email TO primary_email
                     fix: Add primary_email as a new column, write both names,
                          backfill in batches, switch reads, then drop email in
                          a later migration under an MG004 allow.
  4  MG005  error    Renaming orders to purchases removes the old name while the
                     previous release is still querying it.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE orders RENAME TO purchases
                     fix: Create purchases alongside orders, dual-write,
                          backfill, switch reads, then drop orders in a later
                          migration under an MG004 allow.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0049_orders_user_fk.sql
  2  MG006  error    Adding a foreign key to orders without NOT VALID scans
                     every existing row and blocks writes to both tables while
                     it runs.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_user_fk FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id)
                     fix: Add the constraint with NOT VALID now, then run ALTER
                          TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT <name>; in a later
                          migration, which takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0050_unique_email.sql
  2  MG007  error    Adding a UNIQUE constraint to users builds its index under
                     ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, which blocks reads and writes for the
                     whole build.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT users_email_key UNIQUE (email)
                     fix: Run CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY <name> ON users
                          (...); outside a transaction first, then ALTER TABLE
                          users ADD CONSTRAINT <name> UNIQUE USING INDEX <name>;

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0051_drop_status_type.sql
  2  MG008  warning  DROP TYPE order_status is the drop-and-recreate pattern
                     used to remove enum values, which loses every row still
                     holding a removed member.
                     statement: DROP TYPE order_status
                     fix: To add a member use ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE. To
                          remove one, create a new type, swap the column over in
                          batches, and drop the old type in a later migration
                          once nothing references it.

tests/fixtures/sql/postgres/unsafe/0052_add_created_at.sql
  2  MG001  error    ADD COLUMN users.created_at with a volatile DEFAULT is
                     evaluated per row, so it rewrites the whole table even on
                     PostgreSQL 11 and later.
                     statement: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
                     fix: Add the column with no default, backfill it in
                          batches, then run ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN
                          created_at SET DEFAULT ...; for new rows.
